correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=5 the canonical root-vector symmetric-edge polytope in zero-sum H has polar the unit-edge Lipschitz polytope. Central symmetry centers a global maximal inscribed Euclidean ball and gives r=1/max_{polar}||y||. The published wheel vertex criterion reduces its vertices to cyclic ternary rim potentials x_i∈{-1,0,1}, excluding adjacent opposite signs and cyclic 000. Subtracting the mean of all m+1 potential values (including hub 0) yields N(p,q)=p+q−(p−q)^2/(m+1). If p,q>0, the two sign transitions on a cycle each require a zero, so s=p+q<=m−2. At fixed s the squared norm is maximized by |p−q|<=1, giving M(s)=s−(s mod 2)/(m+1), strictly increasing with s. Thus m even has max N=m−2 and p=q=(m−2)/2; m odd max N=m−2−1/(m+1) with |p−q|=1. One-sign potentials satisfy N<=floor((m+1)^2/4)/(m+1), strictly smaller: even difference (3m²−6m−8)/(4(m+1))>0 for m>=6, odd difference (3m²−6m−13)/(4(m+1))>0 for m>=5. Equality forces exactly two zeros, one plus and one minus block; all such extremal words satisfy the facet criterion. Counting cyclic rotations and sign reversal gives exactly m tangent facets for even m, 2m for odd m. Inverting sqrt(N) yields the claimed radii and dividing N by m+1 gives the exact spread. The small m=3,4 cases are excluded. The independent exact arithmetic enumeration for m=5..12 reconstructed polar vertices by tight-edge connectivity and independently verified all maxima and maximizer counts, not substituted for the general symbolic proof.

value.rationale: An exact Euclidean inradius is a natural metric invariant of the canonically embedded symmetric-edge polytope of an infinite standard graph family. The wheel family is geometrically nontrivial and is studied for graph root/adjacency polytopes and algebraic graph models. The result simultaneously determines every contact facet of the origin-centered maximal ball and the exact maximum 1-Lipschitz variance (wheel graph spread); the parity change is mathematically structural. A researcher needing sharp support geometry, comparison with family members or a wheel-spread benchmark can use the precise formula. This is neither a merely finite check nor a known table copied from the general wheel facet classification; the proof includes a real metric maximization and full equality classification. It does not imply analogous radii under affine changes or beyond wheels.
residual_risks: This is a family-specific exact metric identity, not a general graph-polytope inradius theorem.
Novelty of the particular wheel spread value remains a best-of-knowledge literature judgment, not a formal priority certification.
